title: Universal normalized coefficient-system scalar model
statement: Let $(\mathcal Y,R)$ and $(\mathcal X,S)$ be ringed topoi on sites small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], and use their module-sheaf categories and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $I=\mathbb N_{\ge1}^{op}$. For a unital algebra object $Q$ in $I$-diagrams of $R$-modules, let $\operatorname{Sys}(Q)=\operatorname{Mod}_{Q}(I\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}_R)$ be the category of internal module objects [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition]; its natural action makes every transition semilinear. Let $U$ be the exact forgetful functor and $s_Q=\operatorname{free}_Q\Delta$, with underlying $Q\otimes\Delta(-)\cong\Delta(-)\otimes Q$ via symmetry. Relative to a strict reduction model $(B,i)$ with universal counit $c$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower], a coefficient scalar model is a functor $\mathcal B:D(R)\to D(\operatorname{Sys}(Q))$, a left-derived universal counit $\widetilde c:q\mathcal B\to q s_Q$ computing flat-term K-flat representatives, and an isomorphism $U\mathcal B\cong B$ whose counit equation on those representatives is the underlying $\widetilde c$, the exact-localization comparison for $U$, and the symmetry above. No existence assertion is part of this definition.
